# Four numbers, none of them wrong

Sales said 4.1 million. Finance said 3.8. Product said 4.4. The board deck said 4.2 and nobody alive could
reconstruct it.

All four were correct. Sales counted bookings at signature, which is what their compensation runs on. Finance
counted recognized revenue by period, which is what the auditors run on. Product counted anything with a payment
event, trials included. The deck averaged three of them, courtesy of somebody who has since left.

The reflex is to pick a winner. We tried that in 2024 and it survived five weeks, because you cannot delete the
number a sales team is paid against by announcing a standard.

Naming worked. Four metrics, four names, four owners, four one-sentence definitions. Not one revenue with three
wrong versions. Four things that were never the same thing pretending to be one.

The deck now prints two of them side by side with definitions in the footnote. The gap between them turned out to
be a real signal about trial quality, and it had been invisible for two years because we kept arguing about which
single number to show.

Forcing one number would have thrown that signal away. Naming four kept it.
